model: a 70 kg man with the mass-specific field metabolic rate of a free-living hummingbird (linear in mass)

facts_with_sources.fmr_anna: Powers & Nagy 1988, Physiological Zoology 61:500-506: FMR about 32 kJ/day at a mean mass of 4.48 g (5.2 x BMR), doubly labelled water.
facts_with_sources.fmr_two_more: Powers & Conley 1994, The Condor 96:141-150: 29.1 kJ/day (black-chinned, 3.67 g) and 81.7 kJ/day (blue-throated, 8.77 g).
facts_with_sources.popular_figure: Audubon Magazine, 'Where Do Hummingbirds Get All That Energy?': scaled to a human, about 155,000 calories a day.
facts_with_sources.heart: Lasiewski 1964, Physiological Zoology 37:212-223; Smithsonian NMNH 2022: up to 1,200 beats per minute.
facts_with_sources.specific_heat: 3.47 kJ/kg/C classic; Xu et al. 2022, Temperature 10:235, about 2.98.
facts_with_sources.sweat: Institute of Medicine 1993, Nutritional Needs in Hot Environments (NBK236237): 1.5 L/h unacclimatised, 2-3 L/h acclimatised; 580 kcal per litre evaporated.
facts_with_sources.water: Nadel et al. 1974, J. Appl. Physiol. 36:465-471 (heat flow from skin in water at rest and swimming).
facts_with_sources.torpor: Hainsworth & Wolf 1970, Science 168:368-369; Shankar et al. 2020, J. Avian Biol. e02305: nightly torpor cuts a hummingbird's energy use by most of its resting rate.
facts_with_sources.calorie_needs: Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025, Appendix 2: sedentary man 31-40, 2,400 kcal/day.
